case.title: Network room entry on card A-2291
case.objective: Establish who used card A-2291 to open Network Room N-3 at 07:12 on 13 March 2026, how that person came to have the card, and whether the entry followed policy.
case.setting: Interview room 2, Office of Facility Security, Halvern Street Annex. The subject attends during work hours; the interview is administrative and voluntary.

data.text: Can you describe, in your own words, what you did at the Halvern Street Annex on the morning of 13 March 2026?

I was on call that morning, and I arrived at the office just after seven because I was paged about a downed switch. Since my own access to Network Room N-3 had been removed for overdue training, I signed out the spare card A-2291 from the lockbox under OP-7. I used that card to enter N-3, where I successfully power-cycled the switch, and I returned the card to the lockbox before eight. It makes me uneasy to recount these details, but I am certain no one else from my team was present during that time.

question.assessment: An open and neutral initial question inviting the subject to describe their morning activities.

follow_up.purpose: Probe the details of the subject's actions and response to the switch alert before introducing records.

data.text: What did you do after the SW-2B alert paged you at 06:55?

After I received the page about SW-2B being down at 06:55, I traveled to the Halvern Street Annex. I entered through the lobby just after seven. Once inside, I signed out the spare card A-2291 from the lockbox located under OP-7 to gain access to the room. I am not entirely sure if I filled in the sign-out log time column immediately or after I had already entered N-3.

My own credentials for the room were not working due to the training issue, so this was the only way for me to address the switch outage.

outcome.resolution: SW-2B went down at 06:55. Lindqvist, on call and with her own N-3 access suspended pending overdue training, signed out lockbox spare card A-2291 under OP-7 at 07:09, entered N-3 at 07:12, power-cycled the switch and recorded the spare card in her ticket. A-2291 had been Haddad's old card, moved to the spare pool on 1 March, but the badge database still shows his name. Misleading circumstances: the card listed to an employee on leave, her suspended access, and her privacy about her performance plan. The corroborating records open only from exchange 5.
